ideas.physics_build_review: Hybrid SSCB physics (ultra-fast mechanical disconnect commutating into a SiC interruption branch with MOV energy absorption) is demonstrated at HVDC demonstrator scale (Hitachi lineage, L08-052) and at research scale in the non-converged MVDC literature (L08-001/003/004/017); nothing at the claimed 1-35kV/1-4kA point violates physics, but series device sharing, di/dt control with no natural current zero, restrike-free ultrafast actuation at tens of kV, and MOV energy dosage over >=100 operations are all open engineering, which the TRL 3 claim honestly reflects. The 2026-29 path (topology study, SiC interruption-duty die characterization, 10kV single-module demo at an ORNL-lineage facility, L08-051) is technically sound and publishable, but the decisive 2028 experiment costs $1.5M and requires national-lab high-power facility access - the outer edge of pre-company feasibility, dependent on DC-GRIDS-adjacent sponsorship. Hidden showstopper: no finalized IEC/IEEE/UL standard for MVDC SSCBs exists (evidence sec.4), so a first mover must drive standards or sell into pilots without listing. Service burden is utility-grade switchgear expectations. Founder can own relaying/trigger electronics; vacuum-interrupter mechanics and kA-class test campaigns require hires.

G1.rationale: Two independent primary filings evidence the demand wave (GE Vernova Q1-2026 filing, $2.4bn datacenter electrification orders, L08-033; Southern Spirit DOE-backed project, L08-041; ARPA-E DC-GRIDS, L02-034), but no buyer yet names an MVDC breaker as a procurement line item - category demand is one step removed (evidence sec.1). Flips to fail if no breaker-specific pilot RFP/tender emerges by 2028.

G2.rationale: Technical base is accepted-atlas peer-reviewed SSCB literature (L08-001/003/004/017) plus national-lab program lineage (L08-051); no unreviewed academic claim is load-bearing.

G3.rationale: Bounded 2028 experiment with explicit budget exists, but at $1.5M it is the costliest in the batch, needs national-lab facility access, and sits far outside the $25k-250k decisive-experiment envelope.

G4.rationale: Hitachi Energy (L08-052), Siemens/GE named, and evidence adds DG Matrix and Atom Power (P3R2-A-02-S01/S02); catalogued modular breaker vs per-project HVDC engineering and vs SSTs is non-cosmetic, though the whitespace is narrowing faster than the seed assumed.

G5.rationale: Interruption physics demonstrated at adjacent scales; no unlimited-capital dependence ($10-25M v1 is large but staged); demand rests on multiple independent triggers, not one forecast.

G6.rationale: Export path benign (power equipment, generic EAR screening), but no MVDC-SSCB certification standard exists - a genuine unresolved gap the seed did not cover; entrant must wait for or drive standards (evidence sec.4).

G7.rationale: Two independent timing sources incl. one primary/official in-window trigger: Southern Spirit construction 2029/in-service 2032 (L08-041) plus 800VDC facility-level phasing late 2028/2029 (P3R2-A-02-S04); window opens 2029-2030 and persists to ~2034 with explicit window-risk analysis.

ideas.physics_build_review: Back-to-back MW converters replaying recorded disturbances is sound, mature power-electronics engineering (TRL 5 honest; PHIL vendors do it at lab scale and ActionPower parallels stationary units to 10MVA, P3R2-A-03-S04), and the 250kW-prototype-to-MW-trailer path is executable at the stated $600k experiment budget. The build fails not on physics but on product-market fact: the compliance mechanism the product exists to serve is satisfied by EMT model submissions validated against passive PRC-028-1 disturbance recorders (SEL-class hardware), per written regional-entity guidance - so a technically successful trailer has no documented buyer requirement to meet.

G1.rationale: The seed's own pre-declared FIX gate kill condition is met: Texas RE written compliance guidance (P3R2-A-03-S01, primary regional entity) plus two corroborating sources (S02, P3R2-A-03-S02) show PRC-029-1 verification is model-based EMT validated by passive PRC-028-1 monitoring; compliance spend flows to consulting and SEL recorders, and no source affirmatively requires or pays for field MW-hardware injection.

G2.rationale: Technical sources (L08-008/009/010/049) are accepted atlas entries; no unreviewed claim is load-bearing.

G3.rationale: Bounded 2028 250kW prototype with explicit $600k budget exists; the de-risk plan itself was well-formed.

G4.rationale: Competitors named, and evidence adds SEL (passive-monitoring incumbent capturing the actual compliance spend) and ActionPower (commercial MW grid emulators exist, just not trailerized) - the 'no product category' premise was wrong.

G5.rationale: No physics or capital dependence, but the thesis rested on a single unverified market premise (field MW hardware required for compliance) that primary evidence now contradicts.

G6.rationale: No export-control or safety-path issue for grid-test equipment (evidence sec.4).

G7.rationale: The regulatory window (2026-2030 phase-in) is real but opens onto EMT-modeling and passive-monitoring demand, not this product; for the product as designed the window does not open (evidence sec.6).

ideas.physics_build_review: TiZrV NEG sputter coating (<=200C activation, chamber-wall-as-pump) is 20+-year-mature CERN/SAES art (L07-001, L07-037); replication is process engineering, not research, so TRL 5 is honest and the $250k 2027 first experiment (1-m pipes, sticking coefficients within 20% of SAES-class, independent outgassing bench) is realistic on a university sputter rig. The risk is craft, not physics: coating uniformity in long narrow pipes, activation reproducibility, adhesion QA, and lab acceptance-test protocols - exactly what the experiment tests. Production-line capex is modest (v1 $2-6M credible for a coating line plus certified metrology); service burden low (per-part merchant service with quality data). No physical showstopper; the kill risks are commercial - SAES adding US capacity, and lumpy accelerator procurement cycles leaving the line under-utilized between projects.

Build path is executable by this founder (instrumentation/controls core fit); chamber access and OEM JDAs, not capex, are the practical bottleneck. Hidden showstoppers: OEM proprietary data interfaces locking out retrofits, FTO in the patent-dense arc/ESC event-detection layer (correctly FTO-gated), and the CN leg's export-control wall - NAURA/Piotech Entity-Listed and AMEC VEU-removed (Dec 2024 BIS rule) - which removes the named CN customers from the deliverable base case regardless of node scope.

ideas.physics_build_review: Physics and build are fine: pressure-based sensing plus model-predictive valve control to sub-100ms no-overshoot steps is credible - MKS's CMA10B already ships that envelope outside the semiconductor-qualified line (P3R2-A-11-S01) - TRL 4 is honest, and the $300k bench experiment against an independent rate-of-rise standard is well designed and executable. The failure is demand and window, not physics: the incumbent gap is one qualification cycle wide, the buyer (Ichor-class integrators with Lam+AMAT at 76% of sales, L07-049) is a concentrated, high-friction gatekeeper, and the constructed $/tool/year value model spans $15k-$1.4M - too wide to prove anyone will pay for transient specs.

Two-source-plus-primary-buyer bar not met.

G2.rationale: The two cited technical sources (L06-026/034) are atlas-accepted, but the FIX-required broadening of the technical base was not delivered - the thesis rests on an unusually thin technical foundation.

G3.rationale: $300k bounded 2027 bench demonstration with an independent metrology endpoint is well within the envelope.

G5.rationale: No physics or capital dependence; the constructed value model is honest about its uncertainty.

G6.rationale: No export-control or certification barrier for MFC hardware (evidence sec.4).

G7.rationale: The evidence file's own timing verdict: the two-independent-sources/one-primary-2028-2035-trigger bar is 'only partially met' - no dated MFC-specific in-window trigger exists; timing rides entirely on an unmet 2028 LOI milestone.

ideas.elimination_reason: G1 fail (and G7 fail): no primary buyer/procurement demand source exists for transient-spec MFCs - SEMI E17 is 2018 vocabulary, the CHIPS capex proxy is a different product category, and no integrator/OEM dual-sourcing signal was found; meanwhile MKS already ships sub-100ms pressure-insensitive technology one qualification cycle from the semiconductor market, making the window as likely to close before 2030 as after. ideas.physics_build_review: 2-20kW GaN converter design is conventional; the frontier claim is destructive-SEE-free switching at full bus voltage at mission-representative LET, where heavy-ion susceptibility of GaN HEMTs at high drain bias is a known, literature-documented killer - so the SEE-map-first sequencing (publish device SEE/TID maps before module qualification, L09-103/104 methods) is the correct de-risk order, university-facility-executable at the stated $700k, and TRL 4 is honest. Thermal-vac, qualification dossiers, and partner hot-fire (Busek-class) are staged sensibly through SBIR channels. Showstoppers: SEE derating can erode the claimed mass/cost halving (the seed admits this); qualification-file acceptance by primes without flight heritage is slow; and prime vertical integration - already materialized via York/Orbion (P3R2-A-13-S04) and a recapitalized Rocketdyne (S03) - can strand a merchant PPU supplier regardless of technical success. Service burden is qualification-documentation-heavy but hardware-light.

G1.rationale: Primary procurement document (SDA T3TLu draft solicitation, ~40 vehicles, P3R2-A-13-S01) plus independent industry corroboration of a real supply crunch (~100 thrusters/month demand, S05) plus realized buyer behavior (York/Orbion 33-thruster delivery for an SDA mission, S04). Pre-promotion condition 'SDA EP content unconfirmed' is closed - real but thinner than assumed.

IEC 62477-1 provides a baseline certification path (L02-112); China's admitted lack of an 800V safety standard (P3R2-C-01-S03) is both the demand signal and a qualification risk. Showstoppers are competitive, not physical: platform-owner spec absorption is concrete (DG Matrix already inside NVIDIA's MGX reference architecture, S04), ABB's SACE Infinitus and LS Electric's UL-certified 1500V DC breaker attack the breaker element, and hyperscaler vertical integration could bypass merchant shelves entirely. Service burden low-moderate (shelf module with telemetry).

ideas.physics_build_review: MV SST physics is demonstrated - a decade of ARPA-E-funded MV SiC cell-stack and HF-transformer work (L02-033/034/036) plus commercial entrants prove the 10-35kV-to-800VDC operating point is buildable; TRL 4 honest, and the restricted pre-company scope (HF-insulation/partial-discharge dataset plus standards seats, no converter development) is admirably cheap and self-aware. The thesis, however, fails its own foundations: the claimed differentiator was certification-first against 'IEC 60076-24-class standards progress,' and the independent IEC-registry check (P3R2-C-03-S04) shows IEC 60076-24:2020 is a published voltage-regulating-distribution-transformer standard (stability date 2029, wrong device class) with no TC14 work item on SST HF insulation - there is no instrument to be first on. Meanwhile Heron Power ($178M raised, 40GW pipeline, ~1/3 datacenter, pilot production early 2027, P3R2-C-03-S01), Hyperscale Power, Enphase (inside OCP with its IQ SST), and SolarEdge/Navitas are commercializing without waiting for certification - the field the seed said held '1-2 startups' holds at least four funded entrants moving 2+ years ahead of C-03's 2029-2031 product. The $25-60M v1 capital would be committed into a window already being captured.

G1.rationale: Category demand is real (OCP SST track live with public-company commitment, P3R2-C-03-S03; Heron's 40GW pipeline is itself demand evidence; CN 800V adoption per P3R2-C-03-S03), but the specific procurement signal the seed's own gate requires - a hyperscaler RFI/spec revision naming SST power units - was not observed; half the demand-side condition is unmet.

G2.rationale: Technical base (L02-001/017/021/029/030/036/107) is accepted atlas material.

G3.rationale: The restricted dataset/standards pre-company scope is bounded and cheap, but the decisive $1.2M cell-string experiment is gated behind a 2028 hard gate whose first condition has no qualifying instrument to satisfy (see G4/G7) - the de-risk plan cannot execute as written.

G4.rationale: The claimed non-cosmetic difference does not survive scrutiny: 'certification-first against IEC 60076-24-class progress' is void because that standard is published, stable to 2029, and covers a different device class with no SST work item found (P3R2-C-03-S04); and the competitor set is 'far more crowded than the idea record states' - at least four funded MV-SST entrants (Heron $178M/pilot 2027, Hyperscale Power, Enphase-in-OCP, SolarEdge/Navitas) vs the seed's '1-2 ARPA-E-spun startups' (P3R2-C-03-S01/S02/S03).

G6.rationale: Export separability addressed (CN entity with domestic SiC as mitigant); certification path acknowledged - indeed over-relied on.

ideas.physics_build_review: The thermodynamic core is credible: pumped flow boiling, subatmospheric saturation control, inward-leak failure behavior, and cold-plate heat-flux mapping are all testable with conventional thermal-fluid hardware. The difficult part is not basic physics but simultaneous fluid compatibility, pump stability, charge management, materials aging, orientation tolerance, and 1,000-hour hermeticity at multi-kW load. The proposed 2027 experiment addresses the right risks, but its $400,000 budget exceeds the preferred band and a sellable loop would require $10-25M, chemical-supplier cooperation, and datacenter reliability qualification. The moat is therefore a qualified fluid-plus-loop dataset and fail-safe architecture, not the unproven headline of greater than 500 W/cm2 by itself. The 2031 fluid-availability kill condition is essential and correctly prevents a long science project if single-phase water wins the cycle.

G1.rationale: Google's Project Deschutes buyer specification establishes funded liquid-cooling procurement (L14-043), Accelsius has a named two-phase customer and funded product program (P3R2-C-04-S01), and the EPA/EU rules independently establish the fluid-transition deadline (L14-033, L14-034). China demand is efficiency-driven rather than PFAS-specific, so it does not carry the gate alone.

G2.rationale: The load-bearing boiling/cold-plate mechanisms are supported by eligible, fetched, peer-reviewed atlas sources (L14-002, L14-006, L14-022, L14-030); no preprint-only claim is required.

G3.rationale: The 2027 two-fluid, 2 kW, 1,000-hour loop campaign is bounded and decisive, but $400,000 is 1.6x the rubric ceiling and needs thermal-fluid/chemistry partners.

G4.rationale: ZutaCore, Accelsius, LiquidStack/Trane, JetCool/Flex, and Envicool are named; the non-cosmetic wedge is a PFAS-free multi-fluid qualification dossier plus subatmospheric inward-leak architecture, not another generic cold plate (L14-043, L14-045, L14-046, P3R2-C-04-S01).

G5.rationale: No new physics is assumed. Fluid availability and durability are explicitly experimental, and failure to qualify a viable fluid by 2031 kills the concept rather than being hidden behind a market forecast.

G6.rationale: EPA AIM Act and EU F-gas constraints are explicit (L14-033, L14-034); ordinary thermal hardware is separable by market, while final fluid chemistry remains a diligence item. No prohibited China route is required.

G7.rationale: The pre-company loop/reliability/design-in sequence is bounded; the primary official triggers are the US 2029-2033 HFC allowance step and EU 2030 equipment restriction (L14-033, L14-034). The opportunity can persist into the mid-2030s, with an explicit 2031 fluid kill and single-phase-water window risk.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: A buyer-authored CDU specification and multiple implementers establish real procurement (L14-043), while a named two-phase deployment and enacted fluid rules establish the specific transition pressure (P3R2-C-04-S01, L14-033, L14-034). China supports liquid cooling but not specifically PFAS-free two-phase cooling.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: High-flux two-phase cold plates and post-Novec fluid qualification create a credible route to the multi-kW-chip thermal layer, supported by eligible boiling and cold-plate work (L14-002, L14-006, L14-022, L14-030).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: The ODM/CDU design-in niche is valuable and identifiable, but it is crowded and requires long reliability qualification.

competition_whitespace.evidence: ZutaCore and Accelsius are heavily funded and LiquidStack/JetCool have strategic owners; public PFAS-free qualification whitespace exists, but absence of a disclosed claim is not proof of an empty roadmap.

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The decisive campaign is $400,000 and v1 requires $10-25M, both outside the preferred envelope.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Vacuum setpoint controls saturation temperature, seal faults leak air inward, and heat-flux/stability/lifetime are directly measurable; the architecture is experimentally controllable (L14-002, L14-006, L14-030).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: The greater-than-500 W/cm2 goal is not demonstrated for the proposed PFAS-free fluids at datacenter reliability; no verified 10x customer-valued edge is yet established.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: US chemistry regulation is strong; China has real PUE/liquid-cooling pull (L14-035, L14-039, P3R2-C-04-S02) but a weaker reason to pay specifically for PFAS-free two-phase hardware.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: Two independent official clocks land in 2029 and 2030 and remain active after launch (L14-033, L14-034); the 2031 fluid kill directly tests whether the window remains open.

expansion_economics.evidence: A qualified fluid/loop platform can extend from AI racks to power electronics, radar, charging, and other high-flux systems using the same compatibility and control dataset (L14-022, L14-030).

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Sensing, vacuum-decay diagnostics, controls, and data acquisition transfer, but thermal-fluid design and chemistry remain central outside dependencies.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: Largest uncertainties are non-PFAS fluid lifetime, pump/charge stability, incumbents' undisclosed fluid roadmaps, and whether China values the chemistry-specific wedge. Market arithmetic lacks defensible primary pricing.
redteam_flags_for_p5: Require a named ODM/CDU evaluation partner and a fluid supplier willing to warrant the candidate chemistry.
Benchmark against Accelsius and ZutaCore using identical heat-flux, orientation, leak, and 1,000-hour conditions.
Kill by 2031 if no non-PFAS working fluid or subatmospheric-water variant passes datacenter-scale lifetime qualification.

ideas.physics_build_review: The first 1.2 kW programmable heater vehicle is straightforward instrumentation, and zone-control, calorimetry, uncertainty budgets, and blind cold-plate comparisons are controllable within $150,000. Rack-scale and 2 MW emulation are much harder because fluid enthalpy closure, flow calibration, transient electrical loading, and safety scale nonlinearly, but they remain conventional engineering. The commercial weakness is timing and market structure rather than physics: Project Deschutes and Chinese conformance work are already active in 2025-2027, OCP already publishes qualification guidance, and institutional labs can implement reference rigs. A 2030 entrant needs an eligible official 2028-2035 procurement or conformance trigger and evidence that vendors will buy merchant hardware instead of following OCP methods in-house; neither is established locally. The proposed 2028 pilot and 2029 preorders are good decision gates but are internal milestones, not external demand triggers.

G1.rationale: Google's buyer specification is primary and vendor-facing (L14-043, P3R2-C-05-S01), and eight named vendors independently confirm implementation (P3R2-C-05-S02); Chinese standards add an independent market leg (L14-035, L14-039).

G2.rationale: Technical thermal-test and calorimetry claims can rely on eligible, fetched atlas literature (L14-002, L14-006, L14-022, L14-028); no unreviewed academic claim is needed.

G3.rationale: The 16-zone 1.2 kW vehicle and blind three-cold-plate round robin are bounded to 6-18 months at $150,000 with a publication-quality output.

G4.rationale: In-house rigs, NTT/ITRI verification facilities, CAICT/Taier, and OCP methods are identified, but the claimed merchant-vendor vacuum is an absence finding and OCP can commoditize the method (L14-050, L14-053).

G5.rationale: The product uses conventional heaters, sensors, flow metrology, and uncertainty analysis; scale and calibration are engineering risks rather than nonexistent physics.

G6.rationale: Test equipment is broadly separable and no prohibited cross-border route is a base case; relevant standards participation and electrical/fluid safety are acknowledged.

G7.rationale: The eligible timing sources show the core window is already open in 2025-2027 (L14-043, P3R2-C-05-S01, L14-035), not a documented 2030-2034 opening. No primary/official 2028-2035 procurement or conformance trigger is established, and OCP or vendor in-house methods may capture the first-mover position before a 2030 company launch.

ideas.elimination_reason: G7 fail: a good, buildable metrology product is chasing a qualification gap that is already active, while the local evidence lacks the required primary/official 2028-2035 trigger and shows a credible path for OCP or vendor labs to standardize it before a 2030 launch.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: Google's buyer specification and eight named implementing vendors establish real demand (L14-043, P3R2-C-05-S01, P3R2-C-05-S02), though they do not establish a post-2030 merchant-test-hardware purchase.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Programmable chip-to-rack thermal emulation is technically sophisticated but fundamentally a metrology product.

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: CDU vendors, ODMs, hyperscalers, and certification labs are a narrow, high-value buyer set tied to concrete specifications (L14-043, L14-039, P3R2-C-05-S01).

competition_whitespace.evidence: No dominant merchant vendor was found, but OCP methods and institutional/in-house rigs can substitute.

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The $150,000 1.2 kW round robin is inside the preferred band and grounded in a live buyer-spec ecosystem (L14-043, P3R2-C-05-S01). Global calibration: the $150,000 first test is excellent, but the frozen $3M-$8M v1 range crosses the rubric's $5M cumulative-capital target, so this is strong rather than maximum.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Zone power, hotspot maps, flow, enthalpy, uncertainty, and cross-lab variance are directly controllable and measurable (L14-002, L14-006, L14-022).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: No eligible source proves a 10x fidelity, speed, or cost advantage over in-house rigs.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: Independent US buyer-spec and China standards legs exist (L14-043, L14-035, L14-039, P3R2-C-05-S01).

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: The documented window is already active in 2025-2027, with no eligible primary/official 2028-2035 trigger.

expansion_economics.evidence: Cold-plate, fluid, CDU, rack, and protocol products provide adjacencies, but the hardware TAM is small.

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Instrumentation, control, calorimetry, data acquisition, and uncertainty analysis dominate the first product (L14-006, L14-022). Frozen founder note: Strong transfer: programmable thermal test vehicles, calorimetry benches with tight energy-balance closure, and traceable acceptance protocols are instrumentation, data-acquisition, controls, and numerical-analysis products in the founder's core skill set. Eligible technical evidence L14-009 ties the actual product work to this transfer: Studies a multi-layered microchannel cold-plate design for CPU-package cooling, achieving surface heat flux of 206.5 W/cm2 with thermal resistance of 0.1727 K/W and pressure drop of 523.5 Pa in the optimal configuration. Confirmed: IJHMT, vol. 246, article 127060, Aug 2025, authors Wang Zi-Xing a... The 2%-weight judgment concerns generic EE/CE implementation skills, not topic familiarity.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: Elimination is timing-evidence driven, not a physics rejection. Revival requires a dated 2028-2035 buyer or regulator requirement for independent thermal-conformance hardware plus evidence that OCP will not supply reference hardware itself.
redteam_flags_for_p5: If revisited, obtain a 2029-2032 qualification requirement from a hyperscaler, certification lab, or standard body.
Test willingness to pay for merchant hardware versus an open OCP method implemented on in-house rigs.
Do not size the company on the unsupported consumables/protocol-licensing thesis.

ideas.physics_build_review: Low-ripple AFE rectification is established engineering, and a side-by-side thyristor-versus-AFE stack test can measure specific energy, power factor, harmonics, and degradation inside the $250,000 experiment budget. The build risk moves rapidly from electronics to 5-50 MW packaging, grid interconnection, downtime, plant controls, and performance-contract finance. P4 identified Ingeteam already shipping an IGBT AFE product with less than 3% harmonic distortion (P3R2-C-07-S02), while Sungrow vertically integrates the same function in China. The illustrative payback is 6-12 years at assumed electricity and capex values, so the retrofit needs plant-specific proof, not the headline 5-14% literature range. More importantly for a 2030 launch, the US 45V construction-start deadline moved to 2027 and no named US electrowinning buyer or primary 2030-2034 China retrofit trigger was found. The concept is a valid experiment but not yet a launch-timed company.

G1.rationale: China has a real centralized tender and a documented underperforming plant (L11-051, L11-049), and DOE H2Hub awards establish US project spending (L11-032). The policy-independent US electrowinning beachhead lacks a named primary buyer or tender, so the US leg cannot carry the gate independently.

G2.rationale: The ripple/efficiency mechanism is supported by eligible, fetched, peer-reviewed L11 sources (L11-016, L11-017, L11-026); no unverified academic record is needed.

G3.rationale: A 6-18 month side-by-side pilot-stack experiment is explicit at $250,000 and directly tests the claimed savings band.

G4.rationale: Ingeteam already ships the proposed AFE topology (P3R2-C-07-S02), while Sungrow and ABB occupy the category; retrofit packaging, stack-neutral controls, and M&V-backed performance contracts are non-cosmetic but commercially unproven differences.

G5.rationale: No new physics is required and the first experiment can falsify the savings claim; the long payback and plant integration are acknowledged rather than hidden.

G6.rationale: Industrial rectifiers are treated as separable commercial equipment, policy changes and FEOC treatment are acknowledged (P3R2-C-07-S01), and no prohibited cross-border customer is the base case.

G7.rationale: The strongest official US timing fact is a 45V construction-start deadline of December 31, 2027, which narrows the hydrogen build window before company launch (P3R2-C-07-S01). The alleged post-2030 China retrofit wave is not backed by a primary 2028-2035 trigger, and the only policy-durable US beachhead lacks a named buyer.

ideas.elimination_reason: G7 fail: the US hydrogen window is pulled forward to a 2027 construction-start deadline, the electrowinning hedge lacks a named primary buyer, and the China post-2030 retrofit wave is not supported by an eligible official trigger; meanwhile Ingeteam and Sungrow already occupy the AFE technology category.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: China tenders and the Kuqa problem are real, but the US policy-independent beachhead lacks a named buyer (L11-049, L11-051, L11-032).

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Precision DC for electrochemistry is useful and scalable, but AFE rectification is already commercial.

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Large plants have material energy bills, but retrofit downtime and long payback constrain reachability.

competition_whitespace.evidence: Ingeteam already ships an IGBT AFE product and Sungrow vertically integrates the function (P3R2-C-07-S02, L11-051).

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The $250,000 side-by-side stack test is inside the band and directly tests eligible ripple/efficiency claims (L11-016, L11-017, L11-026).

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Ripple, harmonics, power factor, specific energy, and stack response are tightly measurable and controllable (L11-016, L11-017, L11-026).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: The literature suggests meaningful but not reliably order-of-magnitude customer benefit.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: China has stronger tender/retrofit evidence; the US leg is policy-compressed and electrowinning is unproven.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: The strongest US deadline is 2027 and no primary China 2030-2034 retrofit trigger is established (P3R2-C-07-S01).

expansion_economics.evidence: The same precision-DC/M&V layer can extend to electrowinning, chlor-alkali, battery formation, and other electrochemistry (L11-026, L11-043).

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Power-quality control, telemetry, and M&V fit the founder's controls/instrumentation skills, though MW plant integration does not (L11-016, L11-026). Frozen founder note: Ripple/harmonic control design and measurement-and-verification telemetry draw on founder controls, instrumentation, and data-acquisition skills, but 5-50 MW rectifier hardware, plant integration, and electrochemical process knowledge are outside the profile. Eligible technical evidence L11-016 ties the actual product work to this transfer: Energies (MDPI, vol. 17, issue 9, 2024-05-02) primary research proposing a hybrid rectifier -- cascaded modular multilevel converter plus input-series-output-parallel phase-shifted full-bridge stage -- to jointly mitigate AC-side harmonics and DC-side ripple for high-power electrolytic hydrogen p... The 2%-weight judgment concerns generic EE/CE implementation skills, not topic familiarity.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: The technical experiment remains worthwhile. Revival requires a named US tank-house retrofit procurement or a dated China 2030-2034 retrofit program, plus plant data showing a bankable payback after installed retrofit cost and downtime.
redteam_flags_for_p5: Replace every assumed payback input with one plant's tariff, duty cycle, ripple loss, installed cost, and outage cost.
Confirm whether Ingeteam or Sungrow already offers retrofit and performance-contract packages.
Do not use H2Hub awards as a 2030 trigger without project-specific commissioning and 45V eligibility evidence.

ideas.physics_build_review: Diffusion-bonded PCHEs at 20+ MPa and 500-700 C are established, but rapid thermal cycling couples creep, low-cycle fatigue, corrosion, bond defects, channel maldistribution, and code qualification. A 1,000-cycle subscale campaign is a meaningful screen, though $600,000 is above the preferred band and does not prove 20-year life. Manufacturing and nuclear qualification push v1 capital to $15-35M. P4 also found Heatric and VPE already active in PCHEs, so the opportunity is not component access; it is a documented rapid-transient qualification package. Demand is unusually concrete: STEP operates, NRC Part 53 is in force, Chaotan One is commercially online, and a distinct CNNC sCO2 demonstration targets 2028. China fleet-size/TAM arithmetic remains single-source and CNNC may build internally. The product survives as a capital-heavy merchant component option, especially if paired organizationally with adjacent high-temperature components but judged here on its own PCHE wedge.

ideas.physics_build_review: Solid-state Marx/modulator stacks, active droop correction, and modular switching are physically credible, but a 50 kV/500 A, 100 microsecond, less-than-1% droop system still carries hard insulation, parasitic, fault-containment, thermal, and lifetime engineering. The additional 20 kW RF experiment broadens the program and weakens budget focus; the combined $500,000 experiment is twice the preferred ceiling. ScandiNova, Jema, CPI, and CGN in-house systems are real, so interoperability rather than pulse generation is the wedge. Buyer evidence exists in US cargo/beam OEMs and China procurement, but the 2030 timing thesis is not locally closed: the cited order flows are current, not explicit 2028-2035 triggers, and the EtO regulatory pressure premise is contradicted by the eligible 2026 EPA rollback proposal recorded elsewhere in this same S2 cohort. CGN Dasheng's ownership adjacency to an Entity-Listed parent also makes the most obvious China counterparty unsafe as a base case without counsel.

G1.rationale: Varex/IBA filings establish US equipment demand (L05-028, L05-033), and CGN's filing plus a China accelerator procurement establish an independent CN leg (L05-035, L05-036).

G2.rationale: Pulsed-power and modulator mechanisms use eligible, fetched peer-reviewed atlas work (L05-003, L05-005, L05-009, L05-010, L05-014).

G3.rationale: A two-module 50 kV/500 A droop-control build is bounded, but the combined pulse and RF program costs $500,000 and risks testing two businesses at once.

G4.rationale: ScandiNova, Jema, CPI, and CGN Dasheng are named; an interoperable module family and common acceptance protocol are non-cosmetic differences from proprietary complete systems (L05-028, L05-030, L05-035, P3R2-C-09-S03).

G5.rationale: The switching physics is established and the module test can falsify droop/interoperability claims; no single consultancy TAM is required.

G6.rationale: High-energy/dual-use variants are kept US-only, but CGN Dasheng is wholly owned by an Entity-Listed parent group and requires counsel before engagement (P3R2-C-09-S01). Civilian China sales cannot assume that counterparty is reachable.

G7.rationale: The local file offers recurring present order flow rather than an explicit primary/official 2028-2035 trigger. The seed's EtO forcing function is further weakened by EPA's March 2026 rollback proposal (P3R2-C-09-S03), while backlog and incumbent-capacity evidence are already moving before a 2030 launch.

ideas.elimination_reason: G7 fail: demand exists today, but no eligible official 2028-2035 trigger supports an open 2030 entry window; the EtO pressure premise is moving in the wrong direction, current incumbents are expanding now, and the largest named China counterparty carries Entity-List-adjacency risk.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: Varex/IBA filings and China company/procurement records establish active beam-equipment demand (L05-028, L05-033, L05-035, L05-036).

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Interoperable kA-class solid-state pulse bricks with digital droop control are a credible platform frontier (L05-003, L05-009, L05-014).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Beam OEMs and accelerator facilities are valuable and identifiable, but design-in cycles and service requirements are high.

competition_whitespace.evidence: ScandiNova/Jema/CPI sell proprietary systems; interoperability remains plausible whitespace but has no buyer commitment.

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The combined pulse/RF experiment is $500,000 and v1 requires $6-15M.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Droop, synchronization, fault containment, module interchange, efficiency, and lifetime are directly measurable (L05-003, L05-005, L05-009).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: Standardization could reduce service/integration burden substantially, but the claimed customer-valued 10x improvement is not demonstrated.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: Independent US and China demand exists, discounted for the CGN counterparty/export risk (L05-033, L05-035, L05-036, P3R2-C-09-S01).

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: Current order flow is not an official 2028-2035 trigger, and the EtO premise is weakened by P3R2-C-09-S03.

expansion_economics.evidence: A common module family could span e-beam, X-ray, NDT, accelerator RF, and industrial pulsed power (L05-028, L05-033, L05-036).

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Digital control, pulse electronics, embedded interfaces, and instrumentation transfer strongly, though kV/kA packaging is specialized (L05-003, L05-009). Frozen founder note: Pulse-module control, digital droop correction, and standardized digital interfaces fit founder circuits, controls, and embedded skills, while 10-100 kV kA-class high-voltage packaging and insulation engineering sit at the edge of the profile. Eligible technical evidence L05-003 ties the actual product work to this transfer: Reports a 100 kV/60 A solid-state klystron modulator (JEMA/ESS Bilbao/SNS-ORNL collaboration) using eight solid-state switches with custom air-insulated HV transformers at 4 kHz switching, achieving <10 microsecond risetime and <0.1% flatness; Review of Scientific Instruments 84, 054706 (2013). The 2%-weight judgment concerns generic EE/CE implementation skills, not topic familiarity.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: A narrower interoperability module may remain valuable. Revival requires two OEM design-in LOIs by 2029, one dated 2030-2034 procurement/capacity trigger, and a China customer that clears official screening. The demoted market-context record is not used.
redteam_flags_for_p5: Split the pulsed-power and RF-drive experiments; require one business to win before funding the second.
Resolve the exact ECCN and CGN Dasheng counterparty status with export counsel.
Re-test sterilization timing against the EPA rollback and IBA's book-to-bill before any revival.

ideas.physics_build_review: A gas-bearing turbo-Brayton cold head at 20-80 K is physically real, but the proposed 200 W at 50 K/1,000-hour demonstrator requires high-speed rotor dynamics, cryogenic heat exchangers, seals, bearings, compressor-cycle matching, and specialized facilities; $900,000 and $12-30M v1 capital are well outside the preferred path. More importantly, P4 disproved the raw whitespace premise. Air Liquide already sells turbo-Brayton across 25-200 K, Absolut has a 1 kW at 20 K product, Sumitomo and Cryomech bracket the low end, and CAS/Zhongke Fuhai has exported a 2 kW at 20 K gas-bearing system. The remaining wedge is catalog packaging, lead time, redundancy, and telemetry, with no price or buyer willingness evidence. CFS demonstrates the need for 20 K cooling, but SPARC's cryoplant is already sourced and no second open product-specific procurement or official 2028-2035 trigger is established.

G1.rationale: CFS/SPARC confirms a 20 K requirement but its cryoplant is already procured (P3R2-C-12-S01). DOE fusion awards are ecosystem funding, not an open cryocooler purchase, and the file provides no second independent primary buyer/procurement source for a merchant 100 W-2 kW unit.

G2.rationale: Cryogenic-cycle claims can be grounded in eligible, fetched atlas literature (L07-014, L07-015, L07-016, L07-017) using the accepted versions in the canonical ledger.

G3.rationale: The 1,000-hour cold-head demo is explicit and bounded, but at $900,000 it is 3.6x the preferred ceiling and requires specialized cryogenic machinery access.

G4.rationale: The competitor map is now complete and adverse: Air Liquide, Absolut, Sumitomo, Cryomech, and CAS/Zhongke Fuhai already cover the band (P3R2-C-12-S03, P3R2-C-12-S04, P3R2-C-12-S05). Packaging/lead-time is non-cosmetic but weakly evidenced.

G5.rationale: No nonexistent physics is assumed, and staged capex after a buyer LOI prevents unlimited-capital dependence.

G6.rationale: The product is US-only with China license-only; ECCN 3A904's sub-0.1 K focus is distinguished from 20-80 K, while general end-use screening remains acknowledged (P3R2-C-12-S02, P3R2-C-12-S06).

ideas.elimination_reason: G1 and G7 fail: the only concrete 20 K buyer case is already procured, no second primary product-demand source or 2028-2035 official trigger exists, and P4 found multiple mature products in the allegedly empty band; the remaining catalog-packaging wedge does not justify the capital path.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: SPARC proves a 20 K requirement, but its plant is already sourced and no second merchant-cooler procurement exists.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Maintenance-free 20 K rotating machinery at kW scale remains a genuinely demanding cryogenic-mechatronics vision (L07-014, L07-015, P3R2-C-12-S03).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Fusion/HTS buyers are valuable but few, and the open catalog gap is not demonstrated.

competition_whitespace.evidence: Air Liquide, Absolut, Sumitomo, Cryomech, and CAS/Zhongke Fuhai already span the target band.

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The first experiment is $900,000 and v1 capital is $12-30M.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Cycle efficiency, bearing loss, rotor dynamics, cold power, and 1,000-hour endurance are measurable in a staged machine (L07-014, L07-015, L07-016).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: No 10x price, lead-time, efficiency, or maintenance advantage over the named products is evidenced.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: The valid base case is US-only and China is license-only.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: The concrete SPARC milestone is 2027 and no official 2028-2035 merchant-procurement trigger exists.

expansion_economics.evidence: If differentiated, the same engine could serve fusion, HTS grids, hydrogen, and cryogenic process systems (P3R2-C-12-S03, P3R2-C-12-S05).

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Controls and telemetry transfer, but cryogenic turbomachinery dominates.

redteam_flags_for_p5: Revive only with a named buyer LOI specifying a catalog/lead-time gap not met by Air Liquide or Absolut.
Compare delivered efficiency, maintenance interval, price, and lead time across the full competitor set.
Keep all China activity license-only until formal classification and end-use review are complete.

ideas.physics_build_review: Nanosecond GaN current drivers, multi-channel interlocks, and closed-loop pump modulation are buildable, and the $180,000 eight-channel experiment is appropriately bounded. The hard scaling issues are current sharing, package inductance, EMI, diode lifetime, safety, and whether modulation actually improves TMI at a customer-valued operating point. US laser-system demand is strong, but merchant-driver demand is indirect because nLIGHT, Coherent, IPG, Han's, and Raycus have in-house electronics teams. The two-paid-evaluation gate is therefore critical. P4 also found Wuhan Raycus Entity-Listed with a presumption of denial, so Raycus must be removed from the reachable customer list; the China leg can survive only through a screened non-listed commercial buyer and a fully segregated product/entity structure. JLWS's 2028 demonstration schedule and program horizon into the early 2030s keep a narrow launch window open, though design-in could occur before 2030.

G1.rationale: nLIGHT's funded JLWS/HELSI/DE M-SHORAD activity and company revenue establish a real US buyer ecosystem (P3R2-C-13-S03, P3R2-C-13-S04), and Raycus filings establish China laser volume (P3R2-C-13-S05). Neither proves OEM willingness to outsource the driver, so paid evaluations remain required.

G2.rationale: Laser/TMI and coherent-control claims can use eligible, fetched peer-reviewed atlas sources (L12-001, L12-002, L12-016); no unverified academic claim is needed.

G3.rationale: The 8-channel, 1 kA aggregate driver plus university amplifier trial is bounded to 6-18 months at $180,000 and directly tests stability benefit.

G4.rationale: In-house teams at IPG, nLIGHT, Raycus, and Han's are the closest competitors; qualified reliability data and TMI-aware firmware are non-cosmetic, but no merchant buy-versus-build win has been shown (L12-033, L12-034, L12-037).

G5.rationale: The electronics are conventional enough to prototype, and the experiment can falsify the TMI-control claim without assuming an order-of-magnitude gain.

G6.rationale: The US defense line and China commercial line are segregated from day one. Raycus is explicitly excluded because it is Entity-Listed (P3R2-C-13-S01, P3R2-C-13-S02); a different screened China buyer and US-content-free domestic chain are required.

G7.rationale: JLWS has an explicit 2028 demonstration target and funded horizon into the early 2030s (P3R2-C-13-S03), while the 2026-2029 plan culminates in paid evaluations. The window is tight because prime/OEM design-in may close before 2030, so failure to obtain both evaluations by 2028 kills or folds the idea into D-10.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: Large laser-system demand is real (P3R2-C-13-S03, P3R2-C-13-S04, P3R2-C-13-S05), but no buyer has yet paid to evaluate a merchant driver and Raycus is not reachable from a US-content line.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Nanosecond kiloamp current steering coupled to high-power laser stability is a genuine frontier subsystem with defense and industrial reach (L12-001, L12-002, L12-016, P3R2-C-13-S03).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Laser OEMs are identifiable and high-value, but in-house design culture makes the beachhead hard to reach.

competition_whitespace.evidence: The real competitors are OEM in-house teams; public absence of a merchant module does not show willingness to buy one.

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The decisive $180,000 build is inside the preferred band and uses university laser access; v1 at $5-12M is only partly inside the mission ceiling, with the relevant high-power-laser/TMI test context established by L12-016 and the funded OEM ecosystem by P3R2-C-13-S03.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Edge timing, current balance, TMI response, diode health, EMI, and interlock performance are directly instrumentable and iteratively engineerable (L12-001, L12-002, L12-016).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: Nanosecond programmability is impressive, but no eligible source shows a 10x customer-valued improvement over an OEM's in-house driver.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: US demand is strong, but the best-documented China customer, Raycus, is blocked (P3R2-C-13-S01); Han's and other alternatives remain unscreened and uncommitted.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: JLWS supports activity through the early 2030s, but the decisive paid evaluations and buy-versus-build decisions occur by 2028, leaving material pre-launch closure risk.

expansion_economics.evidence: The driver/telemetry architecture can extend across industrial, ultrafast, directed-energy, and other diode-pumped platforms using shared power stages and reliability data (L12-033, L12-036).

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Fast power circuits, FPGA interlocks, sensing, and embedded telemetry closely match the product's core; eligible TMI/control evidence defines measurable engineering targets (L12-001, L12-016). Frozen founder note: Strong transfer: multi-channel nanosecond-edge current-drive circuits, safety interlocks, and diode-health telemetry are direct founder-profile circuits, embedded-systems, and instrumentation work. Eligible technical evidence L12-025 ties the actual product work to this transfer: Compares current-modulation waveform shapes for an LLC-resonant-converter-based laser diode driver and their effect on laser diode performance, a power-electronics design paper directly relevant to pump-diode and processing-diode drive electronics. The 2%-weight judgment concerns generic EE/CE implementation skills, not topic familiarity.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: The dominant uncertainties are merchant buy-versus-build behavior, TMI benefit at relevant power, Raycus removal from the customer list, Han's screening, and whether paid evaluations can happen before the design window closes.
redteam_flags_for_p5: Enforce the 2028 two-paid-evaluation gate; one must be a screened China commercial buyer other than Raycus.
Require a clean ITAR/EAR technology-control plan and ownership separation before any US defense discussion.
Measure customer-valued laser stability or lifetime gain, not only electrical edge speed.

ideas.physics_build_review: Gas-foil bearings and dry-gas seals for 20 MPa, high-temperature, 100+ krpm sCO2 machines are physically credible but mechanically unforgiving: lift-off, rotor dynamics, coatings, wear, thermal distortion, leakage, CO2 compatibility, and fault transients interact. The proposed heated high-pressure spin rig addresses those risks, but at $700,000 it is well above the preferred experiment range. More damaging, P4 found John Crane already supplying sCO2 seals to the Allam Cycle and another pilot, so half of the bundle is occupied. The bearing-side wedge may remain, but product-specific demand is not proven: no STEP Phase 2 order exists, Chaotan One's sourcing is unknown, and no OEM development contract or merchant cartridge procurement was found. The concept can remain an option paired with C-08, but it fails as a separately advanced P4 record.

G1.rationale: Underlying sCO2 projects are real, but no primary buyer/procurement source shows demand for a merchant bearing/seal cartridge. The stated US Phase 2 order gate is not triggered and the China reference plant's sourcing is unknown.

G2.rationale: Rotor-support and sCO2 materials claims use eligible, fetched peer-reviewed atlas sources (L04-101, L04-109, L04-112, L04-113).

G3.rationale: The heated high-pressure spin-rig campaign is bounded and falsifiable, but its $700,000 budget is 2.8x the rubric ceiling.

G4.rationale: John Crane is an already-shipping sCO2 seal incumbent (P3R2-C-19-S01); the remaining non-cosmetic difference is an integrated gas-foil-bearing cartridge, whose competitor map and buyer value remain incomplete.

G5.rationale: The tribology and seal physics are established and the rig can kill the design; staged spend avoids an unlimited-capital assumption.

G6.rationale: Non-nuclear machines are the cross-border base case and nuclear variants stay US-only; no prohibited route is required.

G7.rationale: The paired sCO2 wave has a 2028 China project and US regulatory path (L04-039, L04-113), but this idea's own acceleration gate is not yet triggered and it is killed by 2033 without an OEM contract.

ideas.elimination_reason: G1 fail: project-level sCO2 demand does not establish merchant cartridge demand, the US follow-on-order gate is not triggered, China sourcing is unknown, and John Crane already occupies the seal half of the bundle. Retain only as an option inside the C-08 company thesis.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: sCO2 projects are real, but no buyer has procured a merchant bearing/seal cartridge.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Oil-free rotor support at high temperature, 20 MPa, and 100+ krpm is a genuine tribology/rotordynamics frontier (L04-109, L04-112, L04-113).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: A cartridge is a focused component wedge, but the buyer count depends entirely on sCO2 machine follow-ons.

competition_whitespace.evidence: John Crane already ships sCO2 seals, leaving only the bearing half plausibly open (P3R2-C-19-S01).

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The spin-rig campaign costs $700,000 and requires specialized high-pressure rotating machinery.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Lift-off, leakage, wear, vibration, temperature, and life are measurable, but rig-to-machine extrapolation is difficult.

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: No order-of-magnitude life, leakage, or integration improvement is demonstrated.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: Both project ecosystems exist, but US follow-on orders and China merchant sourcing are unproven.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: The paired sCO2 wave includes an explicit 2028 China project (L04-113), but this component's own order gate is unresolved.

expansion_economics.evidence: Bearings/cartridges could extend into ORC, heat pumps, and other high-speed machines.

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Test instrumentation transfers, but tribology and mechanical design dominate.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: The gas-foil-bearing half is less contested than the seal half, but without an OEM development contract the demand inference is too remote for G1.
redteam_flags_for_p5: Do not revive without a paid rotor-support development agreement or disclosed follow-on hardware order.
Separate bearing and seal economics; do not claim whitespace where John Crane already ships.
If paired with C-08, cap shared test-cell spending until a buyer selects both components.

ideas.physics_build_review: A 250 kW three-port DC converter can test efficiency and sub-millisecond isolation, but scaling to 1-10 MW demands medium-voltage isolation, semiconductor stacking, protection selectivity, fault-energy management, controls, certification, and EPC integration. The $600,000 experiment and $10-25M v1 are outside the preferred envelope. The greater problem is demand and timing. ARPA-E funds R&D and Eaton/ABB/NVIDIA are building 800 V ecosystems, but no US campus or IPP has committed to a direct renewable-DC coupling pilot. China policy is real, yet Sungrow/Huawei-class incumbents structurally own the route; Huawei is Entity-Listed and only license-out was judged credible. Eaton, ABB, Delta, GE Vernova, and Vertiv are moving now, with NVIDIA targeting about 2027. A 2030 launch is therefore contingent on a 2028 pilot that has not occurred and may miss the shelf-vendor design window.

G1.rationale: The US evidence is a federal R&D program and vendor ecosystem activity, not a named campus/IPP procurement; the evidence file explicitly finds no customer pilot. China policy is not a reachable beachhead for a new entrant.

G2.rationale: Multiport conversion and DC protection claims can rely on eligible, fetched peer-reviewed atlas sources (L08-001, L08-003, L08-004, L08-049).

G3.rationale: The 250 kW three-port prototype is bounded, but at $600,000 it is above the rubric band and does not validate MW/MV deployment economics.

G4.rationale: Eaton, ABB, Delta, Vertiv, Sungrow, and Huawei are named and already moving; a protection-first multiport block is non-cosmetic but faces formidable adjacent shelf vendors (P3R2-C-21-S01, P3R2-C-21-S03).

G5.rationale: No new physics is required, and the pilot gate can falsify the deployment thesis before full capital is committed.

G6.rationale: China is license-out-only and Huawei cannot be a counterparty without a presumptively denied license (P3R2-C-21-S03); Sungrow remains under scrutiny and needs counsel. The US base case is structurally separate.

G7.rationale: The strongest US timing source targets roughly 2027 deployment and incumbent architectures are already public (P3R2-C-21-S01). The required 2028 named pilot is absent, while China's 2030 policy deadline benefits entrenched domestic incumbents rather than this entrant (P3R2-C-21-S02).

ideas.elimination_reason: G1 and G7 fail: no named US campus/IPP customer has committed to the proposed direct-DC block, the design window is opening around 2027 with major incumbents already active, and China's explicit 2030 policy window is structurally captured by incumbents and export-constrained counterparties.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: ARPA-E and vendor roadmaps show ecosystem activity, but no named US campus/IPP has committed to the proposed block.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Multiport MW-scale DC power flow with sub-millisecond protection across PV, BESS, and campus buses is a real frontier architecture (L08-001, L08-003, L08-004).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Gigawatt campuses are valuable, but buyer access is EPC- and incumbent-dominated.

competition_whitespace.evidence: Eaton, ABB, Delta, Vertiv, Sungrow, and Huawei are already positioned (P3R2-C-21-S01, P3R2-C-21-S03).

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The first experiment is $600,000 and v1 requires $10-25M.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Port power flow, fault isolation, transient energy, and efficiency are directly testable (L08-001, L08-003, L08-004).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: Eliminating AC stages could materially reduce conversion loss/equipment, but no verified 10x customer metric exists.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: China is licensing-only, Huawei is blocked, and Sungrow is entrenched (P3R2-C-21-S03).

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: The US architecture window targets about 2027 and the required 2028 pilot is absent (P3R2-C-21-S01).

expansion_economics.evidence: A validated multiport DC/protection platform can extend across datacenters, microgrids, EV depots, and industrial DC systems (L08-001, L08-004, L08-049).

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Protection logic and controls transfer; MV/MW hardware and EPC delivery do not.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: Two idea-record references, L02-107 and L02-115, do not resolve in the canonical atlas and are excluded. Revival depends on a named 2028 US pilot, not additional ecosystem press.

ideas.physics_build_review: A 50 kW programmable ripple/OCV-cycling bench is straightforward high-power test engineering, while compressing 20 years of renewable-coupled degradation into 90 days is the scientific risk. The experiment appropriately compares induced signatures with known catalyst, membrane, and contact-resistance mechanisms rather than assuming acceleration equivalence. Greenlight already sells up to 4 MW electrolyzer test stations, so hardware alone is not whitespace; the wedge is a validated stress library, uncertainty-aware extrapolation, and financier/warranty dataset. The $250,000 experiment is within range and v1 at $4-10M is near the capital target. Demand is independently supported by surviving US H2Hubs, Plug Power's commercial activity, China tenders, and a reaffirmed official China 2030 hydrogen target. Hydrogen-market contraction caps scale but also increases warranty and bankability scrutiny, making the test-infrastructure thesis more robust than a new electrolyzer OEM.

G1.rationale: DOE hub awards and Plug Power filings establish US spending (L11-032, L11-046), while China has independent supplier/tender records and an official 2030 target (L11-050, L11-051, P3R2-C-22-S04). Main-agent global calibration: the cited projects and supplier records prove electrolyzer spending, but not a booked merchant degradation-emulation bench. Carry only as a marginal pass into P5; flip to fail without a paid OEM, developer, or financier evaluation.

G2.rationale: Degradation/ripple mechanisms use eligible, fetched peer-reviewed atlas sources (L11-001, L11-003, L11-014, L11-016, L11-017); the standards gap is independently supported by an EU JRC primary record (P3R2-C-22-S01).

G3.rationale: The 50 kW, two-short-stack, 90-day campaign is a bounded 6-18 month test at exactly $250,000 with explicit correlation/kill outputs.

G4.rationale: Greenlight is a direct hardware incumbent and Chroma/Hioki are adjacent (P3R2-C-22-S02, L11-043); programmable renewable stress plus a financier-facing cross-OEM dataset is a non-cosmetic but unproven wedge.

G5.rationale: The bench does not assume accelerated aging is automatically equivalent; the first campaign measures mechanism correlation and can kill the extrapolation thesis.

G6.rationale: Industrial test equipment has no identified structural export block; standard screening and separate China market operations are acknowledged.

G7.rationale: The pre-company bench and beta program is bounded; US hub construction/commissioning persists into 2030 and China officially reaffirmed a 2 Mt/year 2030 renewable-hydrogen target (P3R2-C-22-S03, P3R2-C-22-S04). The 2033 sales/campaign kill addresses contraction risk.

ideas.physics_build_review: Distributed fiber sensing can detect local strain/temperature precursors in REBCO coils, and active switching can begin energy extraction quickly, but scale from a 1-2 T double pancake to a multi-kA, 100 MJ fusion magnet is severe. Fiber survivability, bonding, sampling bandwidth over kilometers, false-trigger control, voltage isolation, dump topology, no-insulation current sharing, and certification all matter. The $250,000 experiment is well chosen because it directly measures warning time and false triggers, but the headline should be sub-millisecond protection initiation rather than instantaneous extraction of stored energy. Buyer spending is real at the magnet ecosystem level, not through a quench-system RFP, and CFS/TE in-house teams are simultaneously customers and competitors. The official DOE renewal decision after FY2027 and CFS's early-2030s ARC target support a marginal 2030 window. Advancement is justified only as a staged subsystem program with a fusion partner, not as an independent assumption that every magnet builder will buy.

G1.rationale: DOE's named fusion awards and US ITER procurement are primary official spending (L03-032, L03-030), while CFS has real external magnet transactions (L03-035). No protection-specific RFP exists, so demand is inferred from a funded buyer ecosystem rather than booked subsystem orders.

G2.rationale: HTS quench/detection mechanisms rely on eligible, fetched, peer-reviewed sources (L03-018, L03-018, L03-029, L03-033); no unverified academic record is necessary.

G3.rationale: The controlled-quench double-pancake campaign is bounded to 6-18 months at $250,000 with explicit warning-time and false-trigger thresholds.

G4.rationale: CFS/TE in-house systems and CERN CLIQ lineage are named; integrated fiber detection plus qualified dump electronics is non-cosmetic, but vertical absorption by magnet builders is likely (L03-035, L03-044).

G5.rationale: The small-coil detection physics is credible, but extrapolation to kilometer-scale fiber, multi-kA coils, and 100 MJ protection is unproven. The experiment and partner gates keep that from becoming an assumption of nonexistent physics.

G6.rationale: The base case is US-only; ASIPP/CFETR is license-only and counsel-gated. No official Entity List clearance was completed, so China cannot enter the base case.

G7.rationale: University testing through 2029 is feasible before company launch. The DOE program's post-FY2027 renewal decision and CFS's stated early-2030s ARC path are independent triggers (L03-032, L03-035, P3R2-D-01-S01), but appropriation and no-insulation substitution remain material window risks.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: Fusion/magnet spending and merchant magnet transactions are real (L03-030, L03-032, L03-035), but no buyer has tendered for an independent quench-protection package.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Centimeter-resolved sensing along high-energy HTS coils with fast active protection is a genuinely frontier safety subsystem grounded in HTS quench literature and live fusion builds (L03-018, L03-018, L03-029, P3R2-D-01-S01).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Fusion magnet builders and national labs are few, valuable, and reachable, but sales are programmatic and in-house engineering is strong.

competition_whitespace.evidence: No merchant integrated product was identified, but the closest buyers already develop protection internally and can absorb the wedge.

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The decisive controlled-quench experiment is exactly $250,000 and partner-lab compatible; v1 capital of $3-8M is near the mission envelope (L03-018, L03-029, L03-035).

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Distributed sensing, deterministic trigger fusion, warning time, false-trigger rate, and dump response are measurable in bounded coil campaigns (L03-018, L03-018, L03-029).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: A large warning-time advantage is plausible versus slow voltage-only detection, but the claimed scale and customer-valued order-of-magnitude edge are not demonstrated on a production magnet.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: The credible beachhead is US-only; China remains license-only/counsel-gated and contributes no base-case score.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: SPARC hardware is being installed now and ARC is targeted for the early 2030s, while the DOE renewal decision follows FY2027 (L03-032, L03-035, P3R2-D-01-S01). The timing is credible but funding-sensitive.

expansion_economics.evidence: The sensing/protection stack can extend to HTS cables, grid systems, test magnets, and other high-energy superconducting assets (L03-030, L03-041, L03-042).

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Fiber sensing, FPGA fusion, data acquisition, power electronics, and electromagnetics are central to the product and directly represented in the technical evidence (L03-018, L03-029). Frozen founder note: Strong transfer: distributed fiber-optic sensing readout, multi-channel fusion in a deterministic FPGA trigger, and qualified energy-extraction electronics map directly onto founder instrumentation, embedded-systems, circuits, and data-acquisition skills. Eligible technical evidence L03-018 ties the actual product work to this transfer: Examines strain-induced current degradation, delamination behavior, and screening-current electromagnetic-mechanical coupling that amplifies structural stress in REBCO high-field magnets. The 2%-weight judgment concerns generic EE/CE implementation skills, not topic familiarity.

ideas.uncertainty_notes: The score is highly sensitive to scale-up from a small coil, no-insulation winding performance, partner access, DOE appropriations, and buy-versus-build behavior. The exact extraction-time wording must distinguish trigger latency from full energy discharge.
redteam_flags_for_p5: Demand a magnet-builder partner before any scale-up beyond the $250,000 coil campaign.
Benchmark against the best no-insulation and in-house protection method, not only LTS/CLIQ baselines.
Require a 2029 architecture review proving voltage, isolation, false-trigger, and dump scaling to a representative multi-kA coil.

ideas.physics_build_review: Hall-array critical-current inference and complementary delamination/thermal screening are credible, but achieving less than 5% agreement at production line speed requires careful field inversion, lift-off control, temperature uniformity, tape geometry calibration, defect localization, and correlation against destructive transport tests. The $120,000 100 m blind-correlation experiment is unusually well bounded and can directly falsify the metrology claim. Demand is strong at the ecosystem level: large US tape transactions and a quantified RMB1.6B/3,000 km China contract with a 20,000 km/year 2030 capacity roadmap. THEVA's Tapestar proves that producers buy/use contactless scanning, while its captive tape-vendor position leaves a plausible neutral acceptance-instrument wedge. The TAM is probably an instrumentation business rather than a huge platform, and the unfetched IEC standards record cannot support the case. China buyer screening is incomplete, so market entry remains conditional rather than presumed.

G1.rationale: The US has named tape/magnet transactions and official program spending (L03-032, L03-035, L03-044); China has a signed RMB1.6B, roughly 3,000 km contract plus independent grid procurement (P3R2-D-02-S02, L03-041). Tapestar's use by major producers confirms the instrument category (P3R2-D-02-S01).

G2.rationale: Critical-current mapping and defect mechanisms rely on eligible, fetched peer-reviewed sources (L03-003, L03-018, L03-018, L03-050 using the accepted ledger versions). The unfetched standards record is excluded.

G3.rationale: The 100 m reel-to-reel blind correlation against 50 transport samples is a 6-18 month, $120,000 decisive experiment.

G4.rationale: THEVA Tapestar is a verified direct competitor (P3R2-D-02-S01); an independent, buyer-trusted acceptance system combining line-speed Ic mapping and delamination screening is a non-cosmetic difference from a tape producer's captive tool.

G5.rationale: The physics is established and the blind transport correlation can kill the accuracy claim cheaply; no single fusion forecast is required because tape QA also serves grids and magnet builders.

G6.rationale: The instrument is ordinary metrology, but WST/ASIPP and Shanghai counterparties were not conclusively screened against official lists. China sales require official screening before transaction; no listed party is assumed reachable.

G7.rationale: The 2026-2029 instrument/correlation path is feasible. Shanghai Superconductor discloses 2025-2027 deliveries and a 20,000 km/year 2030 capacity target (P3R2-D-02-S02), while the independent Tokamak Energy tape agreement points to pilot/commercial plants into the early 2030s (L03-044).

demonstrated_demand.evidence: Named US transactions, a direct RMB1.6B/3,000 km China contract, and State Grid procurement establish volume growth; Tapestar confirms actual instrument use (L03-035, L03-041, L03-044, P3R2-D-02-S01, P3R2-D-02-S02).

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Contactless imaging of distributed superconducting current and latent delamination at reel speed is a distinctive frontier metrology problem (L03-003, L03-018, L03-018).

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Fewer than roughly ten major tape vendors plus high-value magnet builders form a narrow, reachable, quality-critical buyer set, with one producer scaling to 20,000 km/year by 2030 (P3R2-D-02-S02).

competition_whitespace.evidence: Tapestar is already used broadly, but THEVA's captive vendor role leaves a plausible neutral-referee and multi-modal acceptance wedge (P3R2-D-02-S01).

reachable_validation_budget.evidence: The decisive blind 100 m/50-sample experiment costs $120,000 and v1 capital is $1.5-4M, both squarely inside mission preference (L03-003, L03-018, P3R2-D-02-S01).

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Lift-off, field inversion, line speed, temperature, transport correlation, and delamination signatures are independently measurable and iteratively calibratable (L03-003, L03-018, L03-018).

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: Line-speed non-destructive mapping can be much faster than sampled transport testing, but no eligible source quantifies a 10x throughput or yield benefit versus Tapestar/in-house scanners.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: Independent US and China tape/procurement signals exist, including a direct China 2030 capacity roadmap (L03-035, L03-041, L03-044, P3R2-D-02-S02); China score is discounted for incomplete counterparty screening.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: The signed 2025-2027 China deliveries and explicit 2030 capacity target align directly with a 2030 launch, independently reinforced by Tokamak Energy's pilot/commercial tape path (P3R2-D-02-S02, L03-044).

expansion_economics.evidence: The calibrated platform can extend to incoming inspection, magnet QA, HTS cable, and other coated-conductor defects, but the hardware TAM remains modest.

Eligible technical evidence L03-018 ties the actual product work to this transfer: Examines strain-induced current degradation, delamination behavior, and screening-current electromagnetic-mechanical coupling that amplifies structural stress in REBCO high-field magnets. The 2%-weight judgment concerns generic EE/CE implementation skills, not topic familiarity.

redteam_flags_for_p5: Buy or benchmark Tapestar before claiming an independent performance gap.
